==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/tɛst/|[tʰɛst]|a=RP,GA}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-test.wav|a=Southern England}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-test.ogg|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-a test.ogg|a=RP|text=a test}}
* {{IPA|en|[tʰe̞st]|a=AU,NZ,South Africa}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛst|s=1}}

===Etymology 1===
[[Image:Sea urchin tests.jpg|thumb|right|Two sea urchin tests]]
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ters-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|test}}, {{m|enm|teste}}, from {{der|en|fro|test}}, {{m|fro|teste|t=an earthen vessel, especially a pot in which metals were tried}}, from {{der|en|la|testum|t=the lid of an earthen vessel, an earthen vessel, an earthen pot}}, from {{m|la|*terstus}}, past participle of the root {{m|la|*tersa||dry land}}. See [[terra]], [[thirst]]. The ''examination'' sense came via metaphor of the metallurgical sense: the way a metallurgist ''puts to the test'' their gold, a teacher may ''put to the test'' their students' knowledge.

{{displaced|ang|afandung}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|challenge}} A [[challenge#Noun|challenge]], [[trial]].
## {{senseid|en|exam}} {{lb|en|academia}} An [[examination]], given often during the academic [[term]].
## {{senseid|en|item examination}} A [[session]] in which a [[product]], piece of [[equipment]], or [[system]] is [[examine]]d under [[everyday]] or [[extreme]] [[condition]]s to [[evaluate]] its [[durability]], etc.
## {{lb|en|psychology|psychometrics}} A [[standardised]] [[measure]], consisting of one or more [[item]]s.
##: {{coi|en|aptitude '''test'''}}
##: {{coi|en|'''Test''' Theory}}
## {{senseid|en|cricket}} {{lb|en|cricket|normally "[[Test]]"}} A [[Test match]].
# {{senseid|en|marine biology}} {{lb|en|marine biology}} The external [[calciferous]] shell, or [[endoskeleton]], of an [[echinoderm]], e.g. [[sand dollar|sand dollars]] and [[sea urchin|sea urchins]]; [[testa]].
# {{senseid|en|cupel}} A [[cupel]] or cupelling [[hearth]] in which [[precious metal]]s are [[melt]]ed for trial and refinement.
# {{senseid|en|bottany}} {{lb|en|botany}} [[testa|Testa]]; [[seed coat]].
# {{senseid|en|judgement}} {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[judgment|Judgment]]; [[distinction]]; [[discrimination]].
#* {{RQ:Dryden Aureng-zebe|passage=Who would excel, when few can make a '''test''' / Betwixt indifferent writing and the best?}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# To [[challenge#Verb|challenge]], to put a [[strain#Noun|strain]] on (something).
#: {{ux|en|Climbing the mountain '''tested''' our stamina.}}
# To [[refine]] (gold, silver, etc.) in a [[test]] or [[cupel]]; to subject to [[cupellation]].
# To put to the proof; to prove the truth, genuineness, or quality of by experiment, or by some principle or standard; to try.
#: {{ux|en|to '''test''' the soundness of a principle}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''test''' the validity of an argument}}
#* ''' September 17, 1796''', {{w|George Washington}}, ''[[s:Washington's Farewell Address|Farewell Address]]''
# {{lb|en|academics}} To administer or assign an examination, often given during the academic term, to (somebody).
# To place a product or piece of equipment under everyday and/or extreme conditions and examine it for its durability, etc.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=Charles T. Ambrose|title=Alzheimer’s Disease|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/alzheimerrsquos-disease-the-great-morbidity-of-the-21st-century|volume=101|issue=3|page=200|magazine=w:American Scientist|passage=Similar studies of rats have employed four different intracranial resorbable, slow sustained release systems–{{nb...}}. Such a slow-release device containing angiogenic factors could be placed on the pia mater covering the cerebral cortex and '''tested''' in persons with senile dementia in long term studies.|accessdate=23 June 2013|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130424010003/http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/alzheimerrsquos-disease-the-great-morbidity-of-the-21st-century|archivedate=24 April 2013}}
# {{lb|en|copulative}} To be shown to be by test.
#: {{ux|en|He '''tested''' positive for cancer.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2015|author=Leta Stetter Hollingworth; Harry Levi Hollingworth|title=Children Above 180 IQ Stanford-Binet: Origin and Development
|passage=It is probable that children who '''test''' above 180 IQ are actually present in our juvenile population in greater frequency than at the rate of one in a million.}}
# {{lb|en|chemistry}} To examine or try, as by the use of some [[reagent]].
#: {{ux|en|to '''test''' a solution by litmus paper}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|transitive|slang}} To [[challenge#Verb|challenge]] (someone) to a [[fight#Noun|fight]].
#* {{RQ:U-God Raw|page=31|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/rawmyjourneyinto0000ugod/page/31/mode/1up|passage=Back then, you couldn't rock any type of jewelry just like that, because someone was going to '''test''' you or rob you. If you were wearing a chain, you had to be someone who was known for shooting or cutting or knocking dudes the fuck out. And someone who didn’t know you may still try and '''test''', so you couldn't really rely on your rep to save you every time.}}
